entityDescription:
FiberSight is a CERN spin-off that was created with the hope of being the main vehicle for the transfer of distributed fibre optic sensors know-how from CERN’s infrastructure division to the market at large scale.
FiberSight was founded in August of 2021 and our core business is the development of intelligent solutions for monitoring environmental parameters of temperature and humidity, using state-of-the-art technology based on standard telecommunication lasers, optical amplifiers, and optical fibres. FiberLoop is our first project and is the first highly sensitive distributed thermo-hygrometer sensor with kilometres of sensing length. FiberLoop technology relies on a photonic device that launches several light pulses into the optical fibre and measures the Rayleigh backscattering signal that is generated during the pulse propagation. The fast analysis of the pulses received makes it possible to distinguish all positions along the optical fibre with an accuracy of less than 1 metre. The software analyses the changes in all fibre positions and converts the backscattering signal into two measurands at the same time: temperature and humidity/moisture. The optical fibre cable withstands harsh environments and can be buried in the soil, embedded in concrete, or installed in high radiation environments.

We are working together with our customers to develop high quality drivetrains with lowest possible environmental impact and maximum end user satisfaction.

Innovation: Leading or being partner in European or international projects gives us the chance to improve our knowledge and to go beyond the state of the art. New ideas can be elaborated and validated and then transferred to development projects with our customer.

Collaboration: We have a partnership with one of the world’s leading gear calculation software developers. Furthermore, we have a good network in the aviation and drivetrain R&D society. 

Protection: We consider impacts of new technologies on society and environment already in the design process. For us, a successful solution means to satisfy the customers‘ needs and to contribute to the protection of the environment.

High efficiency, low noise and less mass are key enablers for new and powerful technologies in drivetrains and transmission systems. We offer our engineering in the mobility sector - beginning in drivetrains for e-bikes via transmissions for cars and trucks up to new propulsion solutions for planes and helicopters. Aarhus is the second largest city of Denmark, with a population of more than 336,000 inhabitants. It is the centre of "Greater Aarhus", which has a population of approx. 1.2 million people. Aarhus Municipality has approx. 30,000 employees.

Being a part of the 100 cn&sc-mission and the European Digital Innovation Hub, the municipality is committed to ensuring safety, sustainability and support for good living conditions for each individual citizen while at the same time focusing on cost-effective, innovative and ‘smart’ ways of delivering its services to citizens, e.g. urban development and maintenance. Furthermore, Aarhus is very active in relation to smart city initiatives and sees technologies such as IoT, robotics, AI, lidar and digital twins as enablers for creating a good and living city in the future with quality but cost-effective public services. entityDescription: Today, NaviBlind ApS sells a navigational aid for blind and visually impaired people. The aid is called NaviBlind and comprises an app and a wearable GNSS accessory which connects to the app. NaviBlind enables blind and visually impaired people to walk to new destinations on their own, without prior training. Using the product, a blind person can, e.g., independently walk to a store, a job interview, or an event. Our customers are public entities, such as The City of Aarhus, and blind and visually impaired citizens. To guide blind people, extreme positional accuracy is required. Maps and GPSs on smartphones cannot provide this extreme accuracy, and NaviBlind therefore includes precise mapping of routes and an external GNSS device that delivers better than 0.5 meters accuracy. The routes that users follow are mapped using our own software applications. There are no similar services on the market, and we have experienced great interest in our technology. We believe that the precise mapping and positioning technology that we have developed for NaviBlind has the potential to be used in other industries, e.g. rental of electric scooters.

Helix Space provides three services to companies using SpaceTech: 
1. Soft Funding: Helix Space helps Luxembourgish start-ups and SMEs, or foreign ones that wish to set-up offices in Luxembourg, obtain Soft Funding through national (e.g., Luxembourg Space Agency, Belgian Space Office), or intergovernmental (e.g., European Space Agency, European Union Space Agency) grants to develop their product or service. The tasks that Helix Space provides to its Soft Funding customers are: 
• Analyse and identify public grants or tenders that fit the customer’s requirements. 
• Create or guide the customer in the preparation of the Business Plan, Cost Sheets and Financial Model material required by the public procurement agency. 
• Review and determine if there are any gaps in the technical, legal and management material prepared by the customer’s team. 
• Assist the customer during the negotiation phase with the public procurement agency. 
2. Product/Market Fit: Helix Space works with you to make sure your product or service is Feasible, Desirable and Viable. We help and/or guide you through the following tasks: 
• Value proposition design 
• Market analysis and assessment 
• Competitive analysis 
• Business model 
• Go to market strategy 
• Product development roadmap 
• Implementation roadmap 
• Financial model, sensitivity analysis and scenarios. 
• Commercial risk analysis 
• Business/Technical partner mapping & networking 
3. Cybersecurity: We provide the following cybersecurity services so you can achieve your business goals: 
• Risk Assessment using standard frameworks (e.g., National Institute of Standards Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-30, or ESA’s European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) M-ST-80C). 
• State-of-the-Art Analysis (e.g., satellite-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)). 
• Improve their cybersecurity stand via audits based on internal or external requirements (e.g., National Institute of Standards Technology (NIST) Internal Report (IR) 8401).
